verification.reason: AGENTS.md:33 says "TSDoc only on exported package API. Nothing on internals." The head adds `PastBound` with a `/** ... */` comment at installed-packages.ts:18. `PastBound` is not in the package API: index.ts:61 exports only `Install` and `InstalledPackagesError` from this file. A search finds `PastBound` only inside installed-packages.ts, in `Install.read` and the Walk class. The claim also says `TypeScriptMutationAdapter.install` uses it, which the search doesn't show, but that doesn't change the finding. The type is new at head, since the base has no `PastBound`. It is internal and carries TSDoc, so the rule is violated. It is a minor style issue.

const attaches =
			reusable &&
			known !== undefined &&
			known.lenses.join("\n") === selection.join("\n") &&
			record !== undefined &&
			(record.state.status !== "terminal" || finished(record, undecided)) &&
			!(await lensFailed(record!, refused, (id) => harness.snapshot(ProbingDocument, id, context), !rerun));

Choice: One lens task per head, and one adjudication task per head and input, recorded in a root index; a repeat call attaches, never duplicates, and an adjudication the index no longer names records no verdict

Why: A crash must not double the model spend, nor let an older verdict overwrite a newer one

verification.reason: I traced the scenario in code. `Install.read` builds the chain from every ancestor of the module's realpath that holds a `node_modules`. For a pnpm instrumenter that realpath is `.pnpm/@stryker-mutator+instrumenter@X/node_modules/@stryker-mutator/instrumenter/...`. The directory `.pnpm/@stryker-mutator+instrumenter@X` holds a `node_modules`, so it is `chain[0]`. The walk scans that `node_modules` and reaches the sibling link `@babel/core`, which points at `.pnpm/@babel+core@7.x/...`. `#follow` sets `project` to the nearest chain directory above the link, which is `chain[0]`. The target is not beneath it, so the walk records "links outside" and `identified` becomes false. In `reviewChangeset`, `reusable` then becomes false (`listed.identified` false, or `melianInstall().identified` false for a pnpm-installed Melian). That gates off both the attach and `copiesFrom` in `runLenses`. The base decision `review-attachment` says a repeat call attaches and never duplicates, because a crash must not double model spend. That reason still holds. The base revision has neither `installed-packages.ts` nor `reusable`, so the head introduced the regression. The head decision's own claim that "a pnpm store's links between its packages stay inside" is not what happens when the module itself sits in the store. The pnpm test only reads from a module outside the store, so it misses this case. One caveat: the head-only decision `keys-hold-installed-packages` is not a base baseline, but the base `review-attachment` decision is enough.
